record.original_question: In a countable-ball mechanical model for direct cascade, can one choose family sizes n_i, masses m_i, and radii r_i so that energy cascades toward increasing family index and dissipates from the system, and can one identify corresponding structures in an actual three-dimensional fluid?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a countable mechanical system organized into families indexed by i = 1, 2, 3, .... Family i consists of n_i identical hard balls, each of mass m_i and radius r_i, moving in three-dimensional Euclidean space and interacting via elastic collisions (with collisions also permitted between balls belonging to different families). Equip the system with a notion of kinetic energy E_i associated with family i (the sum of kinetic energies of the n_i balls in family i), and assume that energy may leak out of the system through a prescribed dissipation channel at the largest indices (so that the system is open).

Question: Can one choose the family sizes {n_i}, masses {m_i}, and radii {r_i} (and, if needed, initial conditions or a forcing acting on family 1) so that, in a statistically stationary or long-time-averaged sense, energy is transferred predominantly from family i to family i+1 (i.e., toward increasing family index) and is ultimately dissipated from the system, thereby realizing a direct energy cascade? Furthermore, can the families of balls (with their chosen n_i, m_i, r_i) be put in correspondence with identifiable coherent structures in an actual incompressible three-dimensional viscous fluid undergoing a Kolmogorov-type direct energy cascade?
artifact.status_search_result: No literature was found resolving this specific countable hard-ball mechanical model of the direct energy cascade with prescribed family sizes, masses, and radii, nor establishing a correspondence with coherent structures in a real 3D fluid. Standard turbulence references discuss cascade models (shell models, Burgers cutoff models) but not this particular ball-family construction, and the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Cascade model of fully developed turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: A simple system of quadratically nonlinear equations representing a hierarchy of frequency scales is derived from a cutoff version of Burgers' equation...
status_evidence.claim: Existing cascade models are equation-based (shell/Burgers), not hard-ball mechanical models with family parameters n_i, m_i, r_i.

status_evidence.title: Energy cascade - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The process of energy transfer from large to small scale is called direct energy cascade...
status_evidence.claim: The direct cascade is a well-known phenomenon but its realization through a countable-ball mechanical model is not standard.
